stories.title: Storm travel chaos as Typhoon Saudel makes double landfall in China
stories.summary: Typhoon Saudel made landfall in the eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang, disrupting flights and ferry services across major urban centres, including the industrial hub of Ningbo and the economic powerhouse of Shanghai. Ningbo Lishe International Airport suspended all flight operations from 11.30pm on Thursday. sentences.text: Typhoon Saudel made landfall in the eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang, disrupting flights and ferry services across major urban centres, including the industrial hub of Ningbo and the economic powerhouse of Shanghai.
Even though services resumed at 11am on Friday, some 16 inbound and 28 outbound flights were cancelled for the day.

stories.title: China halts rescue at Tibet disaster epicentre over flood risk
stories.summary: China halted rescue efforts in Tibet due to the high risk of flooding from an overflowing lake formed by a mudslide. Hundreds remain missing after the mudslide hit Gyirong on Aug 26, with water levels expected to peak around Sept 1. Rescue teams use drones and thermal imaging but were ordered to withdraw 1km, while over 1,000 people have been evacuated from the disaster zone. China paused a rescue operation on Aug 28 citing the high risk of renewed flooding in Tibet, where hundreds remain missing two days after a deadly mudslide, state media said. A lake formed by immense piles of debris after a mudslide hit the China-Nepal border has begun overflowing towards the area that rescue teams were headed, state broadcaster CCTV said. “All rescue teams have been ordered to stand by in place and wait for further instructions,” it said. Emergency teams which had earlier accessed the area “have been ordered to withdraw 1km”, the broadcaster added. The lake formed after a wall of mud and debris hit the border hub of Gyirong in Tibet on Aug 26, with hundreds reported missing. CCTV said water levels at the lake were expected to rise over the next three days due to continued rainfall, peaking around Sept 1. This increases “the risk of a breach that could send floodwaters downstream and potentially cause further damage in areas including Gyirong Port and elsewhere downstream”, state news agency Xinhua reported late on Aug 27. Emergency engineering teams were closely monitoring the situation, said CCTV. CCTV also said that 499 Chinese nationals and 555 foreigners had been transported out of the disaster zone as of Aug 28.
